components.css: .ds-console{margin:0;display:grid;border:1px solid var(--ink-line);border-radius:var(--r);background:var(--ink-2);color:var(--on-ink);font:400 14px/1.5 var(--mono);} .ds-tabs{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink-line);} .ds-tabs button{position:relative;height:48px;padding:0 16px;border:0;border-left:1px solid var(--ink-line);background:none;color:var(--on-ink-2);font:500 14px var(--sans);text-align:left;cursor:pointer;transition:color .15s;} .ds-tabs button:first-child{border-left:0;} .ds-tabs button:hover,.ds-tabs .on{color:var(--on-ink);} .ds-tabs i{position:absolute;inset:auto 0 -1px;height:2px;background:var(--gold);} .ds-body{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,7fr) minmax(0,5fr);} .ds-log{margin:0;padding:24px;list-style:none;} .ds-log li{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:24px;padding-block:8px;} .ds-log span{color:var(--on-ink-2);} .ds-log b{font-weight:500;} .ds-bad{color:#f08370;} .ds-verdict{display:grid;gap:16px;align-content:start;padding:32px 24px;border-left:1px solid var(--ink-line);font-family:var(--sans);} .ds-verdict p{margin:0;font-size:17px;line-height:1.4;} .ds-verdict small{color:var(--on-ink-2);font-size:14px;} .ds-console figcaption{padding:8px 24px;border-top:1px solid var(--ink-line);color:var(--on-ink-2);font-size:12px;}

narrative.overview:
The console is the product demonstrated. Real recorded engine runs sit across the seam between one dark hero and a light body, and everything around them is plain enough to let the run be the only spectacle. The world is a ledger with an instrument laid on it: near-black at the head and foot of every page, off-white in between, hairline rules, tight corners, one gold accent.

The page tells one story in order: what it is, proof with scope, why it matters in one chart, how it works as four steps of one run, next step. Density is calm and typographic. Content sits on rules rather than in boxes, a serif states the claims and the large figures, Geist carries everything you read or operate, and Geist Mono holds what the engine actually printed. Motion is rich but tied to the run: lines resolve, a verdict lands, a curve draws, a step lights the matching console row.

Conventions were checked against the study of YC sites in [YC site analysis](reports/YC%20site%20analysis.md); go there for the counts. The report separates measured facts from judgement. Read it as evidence, not as a specification: its adoption tables describe the preview before this redesign, and the gold and the 80px headline, above the measured median, are judgement calls.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black hero, nav, closing call and footer; off-white body; the seam between them is where the product sits.
One gold accent; red and green carry outcomes, never decoration.
Hairline rules, 4px corners, no shadows, no visible gradients, no card grids.
STIX Two Text for claims and figures, Geist for reading and operating, Geist Mono for engine output.
Motion is Motion plus short CSS state transitions, and every sequence has a finished reduced-motion state.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only accent. Streak Gold on dark, Deep Gold on light, and no third hue enters to decorate.

rules.name: The Outcome Colour Rule
rules.body: Red and green report an outcome: a check, a result, a stage, a field that failed. They are never decoration and never a button.

rules.name: The Neutral Reward Rule
rules.body: The reward curve stays a neutral grey. It is what a seller shows you, so it never takes gold, red or green; only accuracy on new problems takes red.

rules.name: The Passing Cell Rule
rules.body: The grade scale fills A and B with gold and C, D and F with red. A grade is a Touchstone statement, so a passing cell is gold even though a passing number is green.

rules.name: The Mono Is Output Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono holds what the engine prints or what a machine reads: log lines, axes, probe samples, table heads, the small labels on report values. Console tabs and the verdict stay in Geist, because a person wrote them.

rules.name: The Serif States Rule
rules.body: STIX Two Text sets headings, large figures and prices. It never sets controls, tables' body text or running copy.

rules.name: The Seam Is The Depth Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest or on hover. If an object needs presence, it crosses a ground change or takes a hairline.

dos: Do put recorded engine output in the first viewport and state its provenance in a caption.
Do open with a dark head and return to dark for the closing call and footer.
Do place each proof figure with its scope directly beneath it.
Do separate with 1px hairlines in `ink-line` or `paper-line`.
Do use Deep Gold, not Streak Gold, for any accent on a light ground.
Do keep state transitions at 150ms, use Motion as the only animation library, and give every sequence a finished reduced-motion state.
Do say "training material" in visual examples and captions.
donts: Don't add shadows, including on hover.
Don't use a visible gradient, gradient text or glow. A solid-colour CSS background used to draw a hairline mark is fine.
Don't use card grids or box content that a rule can separate; the console and the demo panel are the only bordered content surfaces.
Don't add decorative icons, feature icons or arrows on buttons; functional marks are listed under Shapes.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading or title.
Don't use red or green for anything that is not an outcome.
Don't lift, scale or translate controls on hover.
Don't set prose or navigation in Geist Mono, or controls in STIX Two Text.
Don't use a radius above `base` or a pill shape.
Don't show a console or chart run that the engine did not record.
